claim_verdicts.evidence: IOrderRepository declares exactly FindAsync, ListByCustomerAsync, AddAsync, SaveChangesAsync. FakeOrderRepository: `private readonly Dictionary<int, Order> orders = [];` `private int nextId = 1;` `order.Id = nextId++;` `public Task SaveChangesAsync() => Task.CompletedTask;` `public void Seed(Order order) => orders[order.Id] = order;`. Code block lines 8-29 match the tag verbatim.

`public sealed class FakeNotifier : INotifier` / `public List<(int OrderId, string Subject)> Sent { get; } = [];` / `public void Send(int orderId, string subject) => Sent.Add((orderId, subject));` — no logger, no other member. Code block lines 6-11 match the tag verbatim.
PlaceOrderAsync: `await repository.AddAsync(order);` `await repository.SaveChangesAsync();` `notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed");`. No other repository method is called there.

CancelOrderAsync_NewOrder_SetsStatusCancelled: `repository.Seed(new Order { Id = 1, CustomerId = 1, PlacedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow, Status = "new" });` then `await service.CancelOrderAsync(1);`. CancelOrderAsync calls `repository.FindAsync(orderId) ?? throw new KeyNotFoundException(...)`, so a found order must be put in place first.

Task.CompletedTask: "Gets a task that has already completed successfully." Remarks: "This property returns a task whose Status property is set to RanToCompletion. To create a task that returns a value and runs to completion, call the FromResult method." Also: "every call to `Task.FromResult(true)` will return the same already-completed `Task<bool>` object."

Second half supported: .NET docs note "In classic xUnit and test double literature (for example, Fowler and Meszaros) ... a *fake* is a working alternative implementation." The stunt-double origin of the name is not in any permitted source: Grep of refs/dotnet-docs for 'stunt double' returns nothing; Meszaros/Fowler are not docs roots in versions.yaml, so they were not fetched.

Order.Id is `public int Id { get; set; }` (default 0). With `order.Id = nextId++;` removed, AddAsync does `orders[order.Id] = order;` with key 0 for both orders, so the second assignment replaces the first; ListByCustomerAsync filters `orders.Values` and returns a list of one.

`public sealed class EfOrderRepository(DonHangDbContext db) : IOrderRepository`; DonHangDbContext is `public sealed class DonHangDbContext(DbContextOptions<DonHangDbContext> options) : DbContext(options)` — a concrete (and sealed) class, not an interface.

Design guidance restating outline item 3 in the lesson's own terms; no documented default or behaviour to check. Consistent with the .NET docs' description of a stub as "a controllable replacement for an existing dependency".

issues.text: Unlisted claim: FakeNotifier is presented as a fake under the lesson's definition ('a real, simplified implementation'), but it delivers nothing and only records calls — in the Fowler/Meszaros sense the lesson adopts, that is not a working alternative implementation. The .NET docs (the pinned docs root) also warn the terms are used inconsistently and define 'fake' as a generic term for a stub or mock, which a junior will meet next.
issues.quote: There are several kinds of test double. This course uses one: the **fake**. A fake really works.
issues.fix: Keep the definition but scope it: 'This course uses one kind and calls it a fake. Other sources, including the .NET testing docs, use "fake" more loosely.' In §5, say FakeNotifier is the simplest case: its only job in a test is to keep what it was asked to send. Add both statements to claims (source: unit-testing-best-practices.md, 'Unit testing terminology').

issues.text: Unlisted claim: 'the way PostgreSQL would'. In the real path the id comes from an identity column (snapshot: `ValueGeneratedOnAdd()`, `UseIdentityByDefaultColumn`) and is assigned when the row is inserted during SaveChangesAsync, not in AddAsync. The fake assigns it earlier; OrderService happens not to notice because it reads order.Id only after both calls.
issues.quote: `AddAsync` gives each order the next id, the way PostgreSQL would, because `OrderService` uses `order.Id` right after saving
issues.fix: Rewrite: '`AddAsync` gives each order the next id itself — in the real system PostgreSQL does this when the order is saved — because `OrderService` uses `order.Id` right after saving to send the notification.' Add a claim citing DonHangDbContextModelSnapshot.cs (UseIdentityByDefaultColumn) at stage-1.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, true for this repo but not in the ledger: the only provider registered is Npgsql (`options.UseNpgsql(connectionString)` in ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs), so an EfOrderRepository does need PostgreSQL. As written it reads as a general rule.
